title: Normalized sheaf insertion calculus at an automorphic point
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $h:s\xrightarrow{\sim}s$ a scheme automorphism, and $A$ a finite commutative ring. Use compatible small skeletons of $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], its constant ring sheaf $A_s$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and the category $\mathcal M$ of $A_s$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For $r\geq1$ let $H_r=(h^r)^*$ be ordinary module pullback: inverse image followed by extension of scalars along the canonical constant-section-preserving map $c^{h^r}_A$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]. Put $(R_rF)(U\xrightarrow{u}s)=F(U\xrightarrow{h^ru}s)$, with the restrictions of $F$ and the constant-coefficient action transported through $c^{h^r}_A$.

For $F\in\mathcal M$ define the $A$-module map $j_{r,F}:F(s,\operatorname{id})\to(H_rF)(s,\operatorname{id})$ by restriction along $h^r:(s,h^r)\to(s,\operatorname{id})$, the inverse-image colimit coprojection at $(s,h^r)$ with graph $(\operatorname{id}_s,\operatorname{id}_s):s\to s\times_{s,h^r}s$, its sheafification map [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], and the scalar insertion $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. For $m\geq1$ write $T_{m,F}:H_1H_mF\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{m+1}F$ for the ordinary canonical module-pullback compositor, oriented from successive pullback to direct pullback.

There are $A_s$-linear isomorphisms $e_{r,F}:H_rF\xrightarrow{\sim}R_rF$, natural in $F$ and in site objects. They have the following normalization: at $U\xrightarrow{u}s$, insertion of $x\in F(U,h^ru)$ at the comma index $(U,h^ru)$ with graph $(u,\operatorname{id}_U):U\to s\times_{s,h^r}U$, followed by sheafification and $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, maps to $x$. With the identification $R_1R_mF=R_{m+1}F$ induced by $h^mh=h^{m+1}$, they satisfy
$$e_{m+1,F}\circ T_{m,F}=R_1(e_{m,F})\circ e_{1,H_mF},\qquad e_{r,F}(s)\circ j_{r,F}=\operatorname{res}_{h^r}^{F}.$$
For every $A_s$-module morphism $v:F\to G$,
$$ (H_rv)(s)\circ j_{r,F}=j_{r,G}\circ v(s),\qquad
j_{m+1,F}=T_{m,F}(s)\circ j_{1,H_mF}\circ j_{m,F}.$$
For every cochain complex $K$ of $\mathcal M$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the degreewise maps $j_{r,K^i}$ form an $A$-linear chain map $j_{r,K}:\Gamma(s,K)\to\Gamma(s,C(H_r)K)$, natural for chain maps, and the last composition identity holds as an equality of chain maps with $T_m$ applied degreewise. Here $C(H_r)$ denotes termwise application of $H_r$ and $\Gamma(s,K)^i=K^i(s,\operatorname{id})$.

proof.text: For each positive power, use the actual constant-section-preserving restriction coefficient isomorphism. Naturality of the constant presheaf sheafification unit proves the coefficient counit and unit equations for postcomposition left adjoint to base change. Mathlib SheafOfModules.pushforwardPushforwardAdj therefore makes the specified restriction functor left adjoint to the actual module direct image. Compare this adjunction with the published tensor-normalized pullback adjunction using leftAdjointUniq. Evaluate its unit equation, commute the comparison with restriction along the distinguished graph, and apply the site adjunction triangle identity. This proves that the comparison sends the graph/tensor-unit insertion to the original section.

proof.text: Extract the direct-image isomorphism and conjugation equation for the exact chosen pullback compositor from lem-pur-proetale-module-pullback-composition. Its inverse direct-image section formula follows by cancelling the forward restriction isomorphism. Evaluate unit_conjugateEquiv on a section: the successive two module units followed by the compositor equal the direct module unit followed by restriction along the inverse fibre-product comparison. Naturality of the second unit and of the compositor extends this to both arbitrary graph indexing arrows, with scalar 1 throughout.

proof.text: Compute both projections of the nested graph followed by the inverse pullback compositor. The result is the direct graph followed by base change of the canonical reindexing comparison. Naturality of the direct unit identifies the corresponding generators. Transport along the power equality to obtain the statement for pointSheafCompositor. Every section of a pullback is the normalized graph insertion of its comparison image, since the comparison is an isomorphism. Apply the generator formula to these images and then the direct comparison to prove compositor coherence on all sections.

proof.text: Naturality of the constant presheaf sheafification unit and the restriction coefficient isomorphism show that restriction at the final object is linear over the original constant ring. Bundle these restrictions as a natural transformation to restricted sections; compose with the inverse normalized comparison. Cancellation of that comparison gives the specified insertion function and its restriction equation.

proof.text: Apply the direct comparison to the proposed composite of section insertions. The coherence equation and the restriction equation for the first power replace it by restriction of the intermediate pullback section. Naturality of the intermediate comparison moves it across that restriction; its restriction equation then gives two restrictions of the original section, followed by the reindexing arrow. The underlying composite site arrow is the direct restriction arrow by the power identity. Presheaf functoriality and injectivity of the direct comparison prove the section cocycle.

proof.text: Apply Mathlib NatTrans.mapHomologicalComplex to the natural linear section insertion to define the chain map, and NatIso.mapHomologicalComplex to the given module compositor whiskered by the sections functor to define the chain isomorphism. These existing constructions supply the differential equations from naturality. Their degreewise component formulas are definitional. Componentwise extensionality gives naturality for all chain maps and the chain cocycle from the proved section cocycle.

Step 1: lem-sfb-proetale-object-inverse-image-restriction (1)-(3) applies with X=W=s and r=h^r, since an isomorphism is weakly étale (Mathlib leaf). G|_W(U,u)=F(U,h^r u) is R_rF, and the initial index is (U,h^r u) with graph (u,id_U). Step 2: lem-weil-sheaf-scalar-extension-ring-iso applies with R=P_rA_s, S=A_s and c=c^{h^r}_A, which is invertible by prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map. Its inverse m↦η(m⊗1) gives the stated normalization. Step 3: lem-trf-constant-coefficient-composition with h and k=h^m gives exactly the definition of c_{kh} in lem-sf-proetale-tensor-composition-unit, because α=a^{-1} by uniqueness of the adjunction-compatible comparison. So that lemma's (kh)^* is H_{m+1}, and t_{h,k} is T_m in the direction H_1H_m→H_{m+1}. Step 4: I recomputed the nested graphs. ψ=(hu,id) into s×_{h^m}U and φ=(u,id) into s×_hU give u(ψ)φ=(u,hu,id_U). The q of def-pc-fibre-product sends this to (u,id_U), which is the index of ρ_{m+1}. The tensor formula sends (y⊗1)⊗1 to y⊗1. Equality is tested on every section x of the source, so no single-representative assumption is used. Steps 5-7 are elementary and I checked them with typed domains: e_r(s)j_r=res_{h^r}; then e_m(s,h)res_h=res^{R_mF}_h e_m(s), and res^F along (s,h^{m+1})→(s,h^m) composed with res_{h^m} is res_{h^{m+1}}; the chain-map clauses hold degreewise, with additivity coming through e. Edge cases checked: h=id, m=1, U empty, F=0 and F=A_s. Stacks tags 03CE, 03CB, 06UM, 03CZ and 03D3 were checked against tags/tags and sites.tex:6094. No SGA is cited.
